assertions.name: bring_knot_jones_values_are_golden
assertions.source: |V|^2 at zeta_5 and zeta_10 for 3_1 and T_{2,5} against closed forms asserted before evaluation

description: Identifies the sqrt5 of the brings-surface chapter with the sqrt5 of the Jones polynomial at a fifth root of unity. At r = 5 the quantum dimension [2] = [3] = phi, and the Bring torus knots' Jones polynomials evaluate to golden-ratio algebraic integers, the cinquefoil's |V(zeta_10)|^2 = 2 + phi being the Fibonacci category's global dimension. Separates this from the c_sigma sqrt5 question: torus knots have zero volume and the hyperbolic closed forms live in the imaginary quadratic fields Q(i) and Q(sqrt-3), where a real sqrt5 cannot appear. Exact radicals throughout; closed forms asserted before evaluation.

zeta_10.reading: 2 + phi = D^2 of the Fibonacci category

three_candidate_sqrt5_mechanisms.1_gauss_sum: sum_k zeta_5^{k^2} = sqrt5, the WRT invariant of a lens space; Sigma_2(T_{2,5}) = L(5,q) since |H_1| = |Delta(-1)| = 5. This is what the corpus states.
three_candidate_sqrt5_mechanisms.2_branched_cover: Sigma_5(T_{2,3}) is the Poincare homology sphere Sigma(2,3,5) = S^3/2I, |2I| = 120 = |S_5| = |Aut(Bring)|. OPEN — needs lawrence-zagier-1999, unreadable here; see qou-lz235.
three_candidate_sqrt5_mechanisms.3_quantum_dimension: [2]_{r=5} = phi and the Bring knots' Jones values are golden-ratio algebraic integers. IDENTIFIED with (1): both are Q(sqrt5) = Q(zeta_5)^+ via 2 cos(pi/5). NOTE the quantum-dimension half is PRIOR IN-REPO work (lr_modulus_identification_sigma235.py, keystone_valuemap_genuine_smatrix_s013.py); only the Jones-polynomial evaluations and the jones1985 link are added here.

what_this_is_not.not_c_sigma: T_{2,3} and T_{2,5} are torus knots — zero simplicial volume, polynomial colored-Jones growth, no Lobachevsky saddle. c_sigma is a different object and the volume conjecture is vacuous on them.
what_this_is_not.field_obstruction: the hyperbolic closed forms live in Q(i) (octahedral) and Q(sqrt-3) (tetrahedral), the two exceptional IMAGINARY quadratic fields. Q(sqrt5) is REAL, so it cannot appear there by that route at all.
